definitions.gloss: either way; anyway; whichever you choose
definitions.explanation: Says that the result will be the same whichever of the options is taken, so the choice does not matter. The casual counterpart of どのみち, common in spoken Japanese.

examples.japanese: どっちみち{間|ま}に{合|あ}わない。
examples.english: We won't make it either way.

examples.japanese: どっちみち{買|か}うなら、{早|はや}いほうがいい。
examples.english: If you're going to buy it anyway, sooner is better.

examples.japanese: バスでも{電車|でんしゃ}でも、どっちみち{一時間|いちじかん}はかかるから{慌|あわ}てなくていい。
examples.english: Bus or train, it takes an hour either way, so there's no need to rush.

notes:
USAGE:
From どっち (which of two) plus {道|みち} (road) — "whichever road." It comes at the head of the clause and often precedes a resigned or matter-of-fact conclusion. Casual: use いずれにしても or どのみち in writing and formal speech.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- どのみち: either way — the same meaning in a slightly more neutral register
- どうせ: anyway, after all — adds resignation or cynicism about the outcome
- いずれにしても: in any case — formal, and not limited to two options
